newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL hopes to decide on Rhine hub by summer.
newsitem.headline: DHL hopes to decide on Rhine hub by summer.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it hoped to decide on the location of its Rhine Valley hub by the summer, Ross Allen, the express company's Brussels-based Facilities director for Europe and Africa, told Reuters.
Strasbourg-Entzheim airport, in eastern France, was all set to emerge as DHL' Rhine Valley air cargo hub when the project collapsed amid protests by residents and political leaders.
The local council, initially in favour of the project, finally backed down over fears of aircraft noise during night-time periods.

During the first three to four years of operation, beginning autumn 1996, DHL had outlined plans to invest $5 million at the site generating 350 jobs. Longer term plans centred on a move into a $50 million purpose-built facility around the turn of the century as traffic volumes increased.

Following the opposition to its Strasbourg project, DHL had been looking at several sites in the Alsace-Lorraine region and the other side of the Rhine, in Germany, including existing or former miltary airfields and commerical airports.

"After our disappointment over Strasbourg, we've adopted a deliberately low-profile, prudent approach in finding an alternative site. Our negotiations with the French government, mainly the Ministries of Defence and Transport are continuing and by June we would like to have identified a site which meets our requirements and at the same time has the full backing of the relevant authorities concerned."
Allen said DHL favoured to two sites in particular but at this stage he couldn't disclose their identity.

"As far as DHL's hub development plans in Europe are concerned, we are about a year behind the schedule we fixed for ourselves. However, the service level of our business has not suffered as a result. Our existing hubs, especially Cologne, where we have invested significantly and Brussels have accomodated the traffic volumes which had been "earmarked" for Strasbourg...having said that, we are still committed to establishing a Rhine Valley hub which is integral to our long-term development in this region," he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
